plain.text: Paul looked straight at the council and said, "I have fulfilled my duty to God in all good conscience to this day." The high priest Ananias ordered those near him to strike him on the mouth. Paul spoke sharply, then apologised when told he was the high priest, quoting the law: "Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people." Knowing that some were Sadducees and others Pharisees, Paul called out, "I am a Pharisee. I stand on trial because of the hope of the resurrection of the dead." A dispute broke out, because Sadducees say there is no resurrection, angels or spirits, but Pharisees believe all these. The argument became so violent that the commander had Paul taken back to the barracks. The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, "Take courage! As you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."

The next morning more than forty men made a plot and swore not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul. They asked the leaders to request that Paul be brought before the council again, planning to ambush him. But Paul's nephew heard of the plot and told Paul, who sent him to the commander. The commander told the young man not to tell anyone.

The commander ordered two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to take Paul safely to Governor Felix in Caesarea that night. He wrote a letter explaining that Paul was a Roman citizen, that the accusations concerned questions about their law, and that there was a plot against him. The soldiers brought Paul to Caesarea. Felix read the letter and said he would hear the case when the accusers arrived. He had Paul kept under guard in Herod's palace.

summary.bigIdea: God protects Paul from a murder plot and promises that he will testify in Rome.
points: Paul's mention of the resurrection divides the council.
The Lord tells Paul, "Take courage! ...you must also testify in Rome."
Paul's nephew uncovers a plot, and Paul is moved safely to Caesarea.
summary.reflection: God used a young nephew to protect Paul. How might God use small or unexpected people, including you?
